response.query: What are the top project risks (data-sharing denials, low participation, service cuts) and which pre-approved contingency actions and alternative data sources will we adopt?
response.answer: Top project risks include data-sharing denials, low participation, and service cuts. Pre-approved contingencies involve alternative data sources and reallocation of resources. Backup plans include leveraging secondary datasets and increasing outreach efforts.

(3) include an assessment of-- (A) the status and effectiveness of current efforts by governments, multilateral development banks, and the private sector to attract investment by private entities who are seeking to diversify from reliance on the People's Republic of China; (B) major challenges hindering those efforts; and (C) how the United States can strengthen the effectiveness of those efforts; (4) identify United States allies and partners with comparative advantages for sourcing and manufacturing critical goods and countries with the greatest opportunities and alignment with United States values; (5) identify how activities by the International Trade Administration and other relevant Federal agencies, as determined by the Secretary, can effectively be leveraged to strengthen and promote supply chain diversification, including nearshoring to Latin America and the Caribbean as appropriate; results.title: FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification
results.content: # Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs  International Security Assistance ................................ The FY 2026 budget request of $28.5 billion for the Department of State, excluding rescissions, will allow us to fulfill our mission, while streamlining programs and operations for a more effective and efficient Department for the American people. In line with the Administration's approach to ending divisive or ineffective foreign assistance programs, the Department will henceforth only fund efforts that can clearly be tied to making America stronger, safer, and more prosperous. To complement these foreign assistance reforms, the Department is requesting funding and authorities to complete the integration of certain USAID programs and management resources within the Department of State.
